## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Parittārammaṇattika* ("Triad on Limited Objects") is a canonical Abhidhamma treatise constituting section 1.14 of the *Paṭṭhāna* [SuttaCentral]. Operating within the analytical framework of the twenty-four conditional relations (*paccaya*), the text systematically analyzes phenomena based on the triad of limited, exalted, and immeasurable objects of consciousness. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in a single language, but lists no curated parallels in non-Pali traditions [SuttaCentral].

Computational text analysis highlights extensive internal structural reuse within the Pali canonical literature. The *Parittārammaṇattika* shares 8,306 passages across 81 other Pali texts, primarily with adjacent and interrelated sections of the *Paṭṭhāna* such as the *Parittattika* (Patthana 1.13), the *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13), the *Atītārammaṇattika* (Patthana 1.20), the *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10), the *Vitakkattika* (Patthana 1.7), and the *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further identifies automated cross-language alignments with Sanskrit Mahāyāna and scholastic texts—including the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*—as well as Tibetan versions of the *Yogācārabhūmi-viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī* (D4038), the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* (D4037), and Sthiramati's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣyaṭīkā Tattvārthā* (D4421-2), reflecting recurring Abhidharma terminology rather than direct textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
